of pyridoxine (Saudubray et al., 2016). However reduced activity of CBS may be only one factor that leads to hyperhomocysteine-
mia in B6 deﬁciency. The folate cycle generates 5-methyl-tetrahydrofolate which is required for the B12-dependent conversion of
homocysteine to methionine and as indicated above the folate cycle may be impaired in B6 deﬁciency. Folic acid supplementation
can ameliorate the hyperhomocysteinemia induced in rats by B6 deﬁciency and methionine supplementation (Yamamoto et al.,
2012). Finally, PLP is required for cystathionine g-lyase activity and PLP deﬁciency can lead to raised plasma cystathionine,
however, this may not contribute to disease as individuals with cystathionine g-lyase deﬁciency are asymptomatic (Saudubray
et al., 2016).
Cysteine supplies the sulfur in the iron/sulfur clusters that are essential for oxidative phosphorylation and this is achieved
through the action of cysteine desulfurase, a PLP-dependent enzyme. Individuals with cysteine desulfurase deﬁciency have defective
oxidative phosphorylation (Farhan et al., 2014) and inborn errors of metabolism that cause severe PLP deﬁciency can show marked
lactic acidosis, for which cysteine desulfurase deﬁciency may be one cause.
